entities.name: Poseidon
entities.fact: In Greek myth Poseidon ruled the sea and also caused earthquakes, and he carried a three-pronged trident.

entities.name: Neptune
entities.fact: The Roman god of the sea, Neptune was identified with the Greek Poseidon and gave his name to the eighth planet.

entities.name: Kraken
entities.fact: The kraken is a giant sea monster of Scandinavian legend, said to drag whole ships down into the deep.

entities.name: Davy Jones
entities.fact: Davy Jones is the sailors' name for an evil spirit of the sea, and his locker means the ocean floor where drowned sailors rest.

entities.name: Scylla
entities.fact: In Greek myth Scylla was a many-headed sea monster who seized sailors from passing ships in a narrow strait, opposite Charybdis.

entities.name: Charybdis
entities.fact: Charybdis was a Greek sea monster who swallowed seawater and spat it out three times a day, creating a deadly whirlpool.

entities.name: Leviathan
entities.fact: Leviathan is a vast sea monster described in the Hebrew Bible, and the word later came to mean any enormous creature of the sea.

entities.name: Triton
entities.fact: Triton was the son of Poseidon and Amphitrite, a merman who calmed or raised the waves by blowing on a conch shell.

entities.name: Amphitrite
entities.fact: Amphitrite was a Greek sea goddess, one of the Nereids, who became the wife of Poseidon.

entities.name: Sirens
entities.fact: The Sirens of Greek myth lured sailors onto rocks with their enchanting singing, and Odysseus had himself tied to his mast to hear them safely.

entities.name: Selkie
entities.fact: Selkies are seals in Scottish and Irish folklore that can shed their skins to take human form on land.

entities.name: Aegir
entities.fact: Aegir is the Norse giant and god of the sea, who was said to hold great feasts for the gods in his undersea hall.

entities.name: Njord
entities.fact: Njord is the Norse god of the sea, seafaring and fishing, as well as of the wind, and father of Freyr and Freyja.

entities.name: Tiamat
entities.fact: In the Babylonian creation myth Enuma Elish, Tiamat is the primeval goddess of the salt sea, slain by the god Marduk.

entities.name: Jormungandr
entities.fact: Jormungandr is the Norse serpent so huge that it lies in the ocean and encircles the whole world, biting its own tail.

entities.name: Oceanus
entities.fact: In Greek myth Oceanus was a Titan who personified the great river thought to encircle the whole world.

entities.name: Nereids
entities.fact: The Nereids were fifty sea nymphs of Greek myth, daughters of the sea god Nereus, who helped sailors in storms.

entities.name: Nereus (sea god)
entities.fact: Nereus was the Greek Old Man of the Sea, a wise and truthful sea god who fathered the fifty Nereids.

entities.name: Cetus
entities.fact: Cetus was the sea monster sent by Poseidon against Ethiopia, from which Perseus rescued Andromeda; it is also a constellation.

entities.name: Mazu
entities.fact: Mazu is the Chinese goddess of the sea who protects sailors and fishermen, widely worshipped along the coasts of China and Taiwan.

entities.name: Ryujin
entities.fact: Ryujin is the Japanese dragon god of the sea, said to live in a coral palace under the waves and to control the tides with magical jewels.

entities.name: Ran
entities.fact: Ran is the Norse sea goddess who was said to catch drowning sailors in her net and take them to her hall below the waves.

entities.name: Manannan mac Lir
entities.fact: Manannan mac Lir is the Irish sea god and son of Lir, associated with the Isle of Man, which is said to be named after him.

entities.name: Sedna
entities.fact: Sedna is the Inuit goddess of the sea and its animals, and in many tellings the seals and whales were created from her severed fingers.

entities.name: Yemoja
entities.fact: Yemoja is a Yoruba water goddess and mother of living things, worshipped in West Africa and in Brazil and Cuba as the goddess of the sea.

entities.name: Varuna
entities.fact: Varuna is a Hindu god of water and the ocean, who in later tradition became the guardian of the western quarter and of the seas.

entities.name: Tangaroa
entities.fact: Tangaroa is the Maori and wider Polynesian god of the sea, and in Maori tradition the fish and sea creatures are his children.

entities.name: Proteus
entities.fact: Proteus was a Greek sea god and shepherd of Poseidon's seals who could change his shape, which is where the word protean comes from.

entities.name: Yam
entities.fact: Yam is the Canaanite god of the sea and rivers, who in the Ugaritic Baal cycle is defeated by the storm god Baal.

entities.name: Ceto
entities.fact: Ceto was a Greek primordial sea goddess and mother of sea monsters, including the Graeae and, with Phorcys, the Gorgons.

entities.name: Phorcys
entities.fact: Phorcys was a Greek sea god who with his sister Ceto fathered many sea monsters.

entities.name: Glaucus
entities.fact: Glaucus was a Greek fisherman who ate a magical herb, leapt into the sea and became a prophetic sea god.

entities.name: Leucothea
entities.fact: Leucothea was a Greek sea goddess, formerly the mortal Ino, who gave Odysseus a veil that saved him from drowning.

entities.name: Pontus
entities.fact: Pontus was the Greek primordial god of the sea, born of Gaia without a father, and he fathered many sea deities.

entities.name: Thalassa
entities.fact: Thalassa was the Greek primordial spirit of the sea, whose name is the ancient Greek word for sea.

entities.name: Tethys
entities.fact: Tethys was a Titan sea goddess in Greek myth, wife of Oceanus and mother of the river gods and the Oceanids.

entities.name: Olokun
entities.fact: Olokun is a Yoruba and Benin deity of the ocean, honoured in Nigeria and in the Caribbean and the Americas.

entities.name: Mami Wata
entities.fact: Mami Wata is a water spirit worshipped across West, Central and Southern Africa and the African diaspora, often pictured as a mermaid-like woman.

entities.name: Kanaloa
entities.fact: Kanaloa is a major Hawaiian god associated with the ocean and ocean winds, and the island of Kahoolawe is linked to him.

entities.name: Umibozu
entities.fact: The umibozu is a giant black sea spirit from Japanese folklore that rises from calm water and can wreck ships.

entities.name: Hafgufa
entities.fact: The hafgufa is a gigantic sea monster described in the Old Norse King's Mirror, so huge that sailors might mistake it for an island.

entities.name: Lyngbakr
entities.fact: The lyngbakr is a giant whale-like sea creature from the Norse Orvar-Odds saga that sailors mistook for an island.

entities.name: Nuckelavee
entities.fact: The nuckelavee is a skinless horse-like demon of Orcadian folklore that lived in the sea and brought plague and blight on land.

entities.name: Merrow
entities.fact: The merrow is the mermaid of Irish folklore, said to wear a magical cap that lets her breathe underwater.

entities.name: Makara
entities.fact: The makara is a sea creature of Hindu mythology with parts of a crocodile and an elephant, and it is the vehicle of the god Varuna.

entities.name: Each-uisge
entities.fact: The each-uisge is a shape-shifting water horse of Scottish Gaelic folklore that lures riders into water and drowns them.

entities.name: Aspidochelone
entities.fact: The aspidochelone is a giant sea creature of medieval bestiaries, a turtle or whale so huge that sailors landed on it, thinking it an island.

entities.name: Moby-Dick
entities.fact: Moby-Dick is Herman Melville's 1851 novel about Captain Ahab's obsessive hunt for a white sperm whale.

entities.name: Jaws
entities.fact: Jaws is Steven Spielberg's 1975 film, based on Peter Benchley's novel, about a great white shark terrorising a seaside town.

entities.name: Titanic (1997 film)
entities.fact: Titanic is James Cameron's 1997 film about a doomed love story aboard the liner that sank in 1912.

entities.name: Finding Nemo
entities.fact: Finding Nemo is Pixar's 2003 animated film, directed by Andrew Stanton, about a clownfish father searching the ocean for his lost son.

entities.name: Pirates of the Caribbean
entities.fact: Pirates of the Caribbean began with Gore Verbinski's 2003 film The Curse of the Black Pearl, based on a Disney theme-park ride.

entities.name: The Little Mermaid
entities.fact: The Little Mermaid is Hans Christian Andersen's 1837 fairy tale, and Disney's 1989 film by Ron Clements and John Musker is based on it.

entities.name: Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Seas
entities.fact: Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Seas is Jules Verne's 1870 novel in which Captain Nemo takes a professor on a voyage aboard the submarine Nautilus.

entities.name: The Old Man and the Sea
entities.fact: The Old Man and the Sea is Ernest Hemingway's 1952 novella about an old Cuban fisherman's struggle with a giant marlin.

entities.name: Treasure Island
entities.fact: Treasure Island is Robert Louis Stevenson's 1883 pirate adventure novel, introducing Long John Silver and the map marked with an X.

entities.name: The Blue Planet
entities.fact: The Blue Planet is the 2001 BBC television series on the world's oceans, narrated by David Attenborough, and its sequel followed in 2017.

entities.name: The Abyss
entities.fact: The Abyss is James Cameron's 1989 science-fiction film about an underwater drilling crew who encounter a mysterious intelligence on the seabed.

entities.name: SpongeBob SquarePants
entities.fact: SpongeBob SquarePants is the cartoon series created by Stephen Hillenburg, a marine biology teacher, that first aired in 1999.

entities.name: Moana
entities.fact: Moana is Disney's 2016 animated film, directed by Ron Clements and John Musker, about a Polynesian girl who sails across the ocean to save her island.

entities.name: The Hunt for Red October
entities.fact: The Hunt for Red October is Tom Clancy's 1984 novel, filmed by John McTiernan in 1990, about a Soviet submarine captain who may be defecting.

entities.name: Das Boot
entities.fact: Das Boot is Wolfgang Petersen's 1981 film, based on Lothar-Günther Buchheim's 1973 novel, about a German U-boat crew in the Second World War.

entities.name: Master and Commander
aliases: Master and Commander The Far Side of the World
entities.fact: Master and Commander is the 1969 first novel of Patrick O'Brian's Aubrey and Maturin series, and Peter Weir's 2003 film is based on the series.

entities.name: Life of Pi
entities.fact: Life of Pi is Yann Martel's 2001 novel, filmed by Ang Lee in 2012, about a boy stranded in a lifeboat with a Bengal tiger.

entities.name: The Poseidon Adventure
entities.fact: The Poseidon Adventure is a 1972 film directed by Ronald Neame, from Paul Gallico's 1969 novel, about survivors of a liner capsized by a giant wave.

entities.name: Kon-Tiki
entities.fact: Kon-Tiki is Thor Heyerdahl's 1948 book about his 1947 balsa-raft voyage across the Pacific, and its 1950 documentary won an Academy Award.

entities.name: The Perfect Storm
entities.fact: The Perfect Storm is Sebastian Junger's 1997 book about the loss of the fishing boat Andrea Gail, filmed by Wolfgang Petersen in 2000.

entities.name: The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou
entities.fact: The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou is Wes Anderson's 2004 comedy about an oceanographer and filmmaker in the style of Jacques Cousteau.

entities.name: The Odyssey
entities.fact: The Odyssey is Homer's ancient Greek epic poem about Odysseus's ten-year voyage home from Troy, much of it spent at sea.

entities.name: Waterworld
entities.fact: Waterworld is Kevin Reynolds's 1995 film, set in a future where the polar ice has melted and the Earth is covered by ocean.

entities.name: Open Water
entities.fact: Open Water is Chris Kentis's 2003 thriller about two scuba divers accidentally left behind in shark-filled seas, inspired by a real incident.

entities.name: All Is Lost
entities.fact: All Is Lost is J. C. Chandor's 2013 film in which Robert Redford plays a lone sailor with almost no dialogue, whose yacht is wrecked in the Indian Ocean.

entities.name: Ponyo
entities.fact: Ponyo is Hayao Miyazaki's 2008 animated film about a goldfish princess who wants to become human, loosely inspired by The Little Mermaid.

entities.name: U-571
entities.fact: U-571 is a 2000 film directed by Jonathan Mostow about American sailors who seize a German submarine to capture an Enigma machine.

entities.name: Crimson Tide
entities.fact: Crimson Tide is Tony Scott's 1995 film about a clash of wills between two officers aboard a nuclear submarine.

entities.name: Voyage to the Bottom of the Sea
entities.fact: Voyage to the Bottom of the Sea was an Irwin Allen film in 1961 that became a television series from 1964, set aboard the research submarine Seaview.

entities.name: SeaQuest DSV
entities.fact: SeaQuest DSV was an American television series that began in 1993, set aboard a futuristic submarine exploring the oceans.

entities.name: The Love Boat
entities.fact: The Love Boat was an American television series that began in 1977, following the crew and passengers of a cruise ship.

entities.name: Deadliest Catch
entities.fact: Deadliest Catch is a documentary television series, first aired in 2005, following crab fishermen working in the Bering Sea.

entities.name: Mutiny on the Bounty
entities.fact: Mutiny on the Bounty is a 1932 novel by Charles Nordhoff and James Norman Hall, and the 1935 film starred Charles Laughton as Captain Bligh.

entities.name: The Sea-Wolf
entities.fact: The Sea-Wolf is Jack London's 1904 novel about a scholar rescued by the brutal sealing-ship captain Wolf Larsen.

entities.name: Captains Courageous
entities.fact: Captains Courageous is Rudyard Kipling's 1897 novel about a spoilt rich boy who falls off a liner and is rescued by Grand Banks fishermen.

entities.name: The Cruel Sea
entities.fact: The Cruel Sea is Nicholas Monsarrat's 1951 novel about the crew of a British Royal Navy escort ship in the Battle of the Atlantic.

entities.name: The Caine Mutiny
entities.fact: The Caine Mutiny is Herman Wouk's 1951 novel, a Pulitzer Prize winner, about a naval mutiny against an unstable captain.

entities.name: Billy Budd
entities.fact: Billy Budd is Herman Melville's novella about a young sailor on a warship, left unfinished at his death in 1891 and published in 1924.

entities.name: Horatio Hornblower
entities.fact: Horatio Hornblower is C. S. Forester's naval hero, who first appeared in a 1937 novel and was later played by Ioan Gruffudd in a 1998 television series.

entities.name: Captain Phillips
entities.fact: Captain Phillips is Paul Greengrass's 2013 film based on the 2009 hijacking of the container ship Maersk Alabama by Somali pirates.

entities.name: Dead Calm
entities.fact: Dead Calm is a 1989 film by Phillip Noyce, based on Charles Williams's 1963 novel, about a couple at sea who rescue a dangerous stranger.

entities.name: In the Heart of the Sea
entities.fact: In the Heart of the Sea is Nathaniel Philbrick's 2000 book about the whaleship Essex, sunk by a sperm whale in 1820, and Ron Howard filmed it in 2015.

entities.name: One Piece
entities.fact: One Piece is Eiichiro Oda's manga, begun in 1997, about a boy called Luffy and his pirate crew searching the Grand Line for treasure.

entities.name: The Sea Beast
entities.fact: The Sea Beast is a 2022 Netflix animated film directed by Chris Williams, about a monster hunter and a girl who befriend a sea creature.

entities.name: Black Sails
entities.fact: Black Sails is a television series that ran from 2014 to 2017 and serves as a prequel to Treasure Island, set among pirates of the Caribbean.

entities.name: Two Years Before the Mast
entities.fact: Two Years Before the Mast is Richard Henry Dana Jr.'s 1840 memoir of his voyage as a common sailor from Boston to California.

entities.name: The Last Voyage of the Demeter
entities.fact: The Last Voyage of the Demeter is a 2023 horror film by Andre Ovredal, adapted from a chapter of Bram Stoker's Dracula about a doomed ship.

entities.name: The Pirates! In an Adventure with Scientists!
entities.fact: The Pirates! In an Adventure with Scientists! is a 2012 stop-motion film from Aardman, directed by Peter Lord, featuring a bumbling pirate captain.

entities.name: The Secret of the Unicorn
entities.fact: The Secret of the Unicorn is Hergé's 1943 Tintin comic album in which Tintin follows clues to a lost pirate treasure from a model ship.

entities.name: The Silent World
entities.fact: The Silent World is Jacques Cousteau's 1953 book and the 1956 documentary film he co-directed with Louis Malle, which won the Palme d'Or at Cannes.

entities.name: Blackbeard
entities.fact: Blackbeard, whose real name was probably Edward Teach, terrorised the Caribbean and American coast until he was killed off North Carolina in 1718.

entities.name: Captain Jack Sparrow
entities.fact: Captain Jack Sparrow is the fictional pirate of the Pirates of the Caribbean films, played by Johnny Depp.

entities.name: Captain Hook
entities.fact: Captain Hook is J. M. Barrie's fictional pirate captain from Peter Pan, whose hand was bitten off by a crocodile.

entities.name: Captain Kidd
entities.fact: William Kidd was a Scottish privateer who was hanged for piracy in London in 1701, and his supposed buried treasure became legendary.

entities.name: Long John Silver
entities.fact: Long John Silver is the one-legged pirate cook of Robert Louis Stevenson's Treasure Island, who is usually shown with a parrot on his shoulder.

entities.name: Ching Shih
entities.fact: Ching Shih commanded the Red Flag Fleet of thousands of pirates in early nineteenth-century China, and she retired with her fortune after accepting an amnesty in 1810.

entities.name: Anne Bonny
entities.fact: Anne Bonny was an Irish-born pirate who sailed with Calico Jack Rackham and was captured in 1720 alongside Mary Read.

entities.name: Henry Morgan
entities.fact: Henry Morgan was a Welsh privateer who sacked Panama in 1671 and later became lieutenant governor of Jamaica.

entities.name: Calico Jack
entities.fact: Calico Jack Rackham is credited with the skull-and-crossed-swords flag and sailed with Anne Bonny and Mary Read before being hanged in 1720.

entities.name: Mary Read
entities.fact: Mary Read was an English pirate who disguised herself as a man for much of her life and sailed in Calico Jack's crew.

entities.name: Bartholomew Roberts
entities.fact: Bartholomew Roberts, known as Black Bart, captured around 400 ships in a few years and was one of the most successful pirates of all time.

entities.name: Stede Bonnet
entities.fact: Stede Bonnet was a wealthy Barbados landowner who became a pirate, earning the nickname the Gentleman Pirate, and was hanged in 1718.

entities.name: Jean Lafitte
entities.fact: Jean Lafitte was a privateer based in Louisiana who helped Andrew Jackson defend New Orleans in 1815.

entities.name: Grace O'Malley
entities.fact: Grace O'Malley was a sixteenth-century Irish clan leader and sea captain who met Queen Elizabeth I in 1593.

entities.name: Hayreddin Barbarossa
entities.fact: Hayreddin Barbarossa was an Ottoman corsair who became the sultan's grand admiral and won the Battle of Preveza in 1538.

entities.name: Henry Every
entities.fact: Henry Every captured the Mughal treasure ship Ganj-i-Sawai in 1695, in one of the richest pirate hauls ever.

entities.name: William Dampier
entities.fact: William Dampier was an English buccaneer and explorer who circumnavigated the globe three times and described parts of Australia.

entities.name: Samuel Bellamy
entities.fact: Samuel Bellamy captured the slave ship Whydah in 1717 and was lost when she wrecked off Cape Cod weeks later.

entities.name: Benjamin Hornigold
entities.fact: Benjamin Hornigold was a leading Bahamas pirate who mentored Blackbeard and later accepted a pardon to hunt other pirates.

entities.name: Charles Vane
entities.fact: Charles Vane was a Bahamas pirate who refused the royal pardon of 1718 and was hanged in Jamaica in 1721.

entities.name: Edward England
entities.fact: Edward England was an Irish pirate who raided off West Africa and the Indian Ocean before being marooned by his own crew in 1720.

entities.name: Thomas Tew
entities.fact: Thomas Tew pioneered the Pirate Round, sailing from the Americas to raid ships in the Red Sea in the 1690s.

entities.name: Howell Davis
entities.fact: Howell Davis was a Welsh pirate who captured ships off West Africa by trickery, and Bartholomew Roberts took over his crew after he died in 1719.

entities.name: Francois l'Olonnais
entities.fact: Francois l'Olonnais was a feared French buccaneer who raided Spanish towns in the 1660s, including Maracaibo.

entities.name: Piet Heyn
entities.fact: Piet Heyn was a Dutch privateer who captured a Spanish silver fleet at Matanzas Bay in 1628.

entities.name: Robert Surcouf
entities.fact: Robert Surcouf was a French privateer who captured dozens of British ships in the Indian Ocean around 1800.

entities.name: Dragut
entities.fact: Dragut was an Ottoman corsair and naval commander who ruled Tripoli and died during the Great Siege of Malta in 1565.

entities.name: Jack Ward
entities.fact: Jack Ward was an English pirate who turned to the Barbary coast and became a leading corsair at Tunis in the early seventeenth century.

entities.name: Olivier Levasseur
entities.fact: Olivier Levasseur, known as La Buse, was hanged on Reunion Island in 1730 and is said to have thrown a coded treasure clue into the crowd.

entities.name: Christopher Condent
entities.fact: Christopher Condent raided around the Indian Ocean in about 1718 to 1720 and then took a pardon and settled in France.

entities.name: George Lowther
entities.fact: George Lowther was a pirate who took command of a ship through mutiny in 1721 and raided shipping in the Caribbean.

entities.name: Edward Low
entities.fact: Edward Low was an English pirate of the early 1720s notorious for his extreme cruelty.

entities.name: Thomas Anstis
entities.fact: Thomas Anstis sailed under Bartholomew Roberts before breaking away to lead his own pirate crew around 1721.

entities.name: Israel Hands
entities.fact: Israel Hands was Blackbeard's gunner or captain who was shot in the knee by him in 1718, and Treasure Island borrowed his name.

entities.name: Laurens de Graaf
entities.fact: Laurens de Graaf was a Dutch buccaneer who sacked Veracruz in 1683 and later served the French Crown.

entities.name: Rock Brasiliano
entities.fact: Rock Brasiliano was a Dutch buccaneer who raided Spanish shipping out of Jamaica in the 1670s and was known for his cruelty.

entities.name: Sayyida al Hurra
entities.fact: Sayyida al Hurra was the governor of Tetouan in Morocco who controlled piracy in the western Mediterranean in the 1500s, in alliance with Barbarossa.

entities.name: Turgut Reis
entities.fact: Turgut Reis was an Ottoman corsair and admiral who was killed during the Great Siege of Malta in 1565.

entities.name: Uluj Ali
entities.fact: Uluj Ali was a Calabrian-born Ottoman corsair who became grand admiral and escaped the defeat at Lepanto in 1571.

entities.name: Klaus Stortebeker
entities.fact: Klaus Stortebeker was a leader of the Victual Brothers, northern German pirates, said to have been executed in Hamburg around 1401.

entities.name: Jean Bart
entities.fact: Jean Bart was a Dunkirk privateer who became a celebrated French naval officer under Louis XIV.

entities.name: Henry Jennings
entities.fact: Henry Jennings was a Jamaican privateer turned pirate who raided the camp of Spanish salvors working the wrecked 1715 treasure fleet.

entities.name: William Fly
entities.fact: William Fly was an English pirate who was hanged in Boston in 1726 after capturing several ships off the American coast.

entities.name: Bartholomew Sharp
entities.fact: Bartholomew Sharp was an English buccaneer who raided the Pacific coast of Spanish America in 1680 and captured a Spanish book of sea charts.

entities.name: Woodes Rogers
entities.fact: Woodes Rogers was an English privateer who rescued Alexander Selkirk in 1709 and later became governor of the Bahamas, cracking down on pirates.

entities.name: Thomas Cavendish
entities.fact: Thomas Cavendish was an English privateer who circumnavigated the globe in 1586 to 1588, raiding Spanish ships and settlements on the way.

entities.name: Eustace the Monk
entities.fact: Eustace the Monk, a former Benedictine monk turned pirate, served King John and was beheaded after the Battle of Sandwich in 1217.

entities.name: Horatio Nelson
entities.fact: Horatio Nelson won the Battle of Trafalgar in 1805 and was killed by a French sniper's bullet during the fighting.

entities.name: Chester Nimitz
entities.fact: Chester Nimitz commanded the United States Pacific Fleet through most of the Second World War and signed Japan's surrender for the United States in 1945.

entities.name: Isoroku Yamamoto
entities.fact: Isoroku Yamamoto planned the attack on Pearl Harbor and was killed in 1943 when American fighters shot down his aircraft.

entities.name: Grace Hopper
entities.fact: Grace Hopper was a rear admiral in the United States Navy and a computing pioneer who helped develop the COBOL programming language.

entities.name: John Paul Jones
entities.fact: John Paul Jones, a founder of the American navy, captured HMS Serapis in 1779 in a battle in which he is said to have vowed that he had not yet begun to fight.

entities.name: David Farragut
entities.fact: David Farragut was the first admiral of the United States Navy and led the Union fleet to victory at Mobile Bay in 1864.

entities.name: Karl Donitz
entities.fact: Karl Donitz directed Germany's U-boat campaign in the Second World War and briefly led Germany after Hitler's death in 1945.

entities.name: Hyman Rickover
entities.fact: Hyman Rickover drove the development of nuclear-powered ships and is known as the father of the nuclear navy.

entities.name: William Halsey
entities.fact: William Halsey commanded the United States Third Fleet in the Pacific in the Second World War and was nicknamed Bull.

entities.name: Togo Heihachiro
entities.fact: Togo Heihachiro led the Japanese fleet that destroyed the Russian fleet at Tsushima in 1905.

entities.name: Themistocles
entities.fact: Themistocles was the Athenian leader who built up Athens's navy and commanded the Greek fleet to victory at Salamis in 480 BC.

entities.name: Yi Sun-sin
entities.fact: Yi Sun-sin was a Korean admiral who defeated far larger Japanese fleets in the 1590s, partly with his armoured turtle ships.

entities.name: John Jellicoe
entities.fact: John Jellicoe commanded the British Grand Fleet at the Battle of Jutland in 1916.

entities.name: Raymond Spruance
entities.fact: Raymond Spruance commanded the American carrier forces at the Battle of Midway in 1942 and at the Battle of the Philippine Sea in 1944.

entities.name: Ernest King
entities.fact: Ernest King was commander in chief of the United States Fleet and Chief of Naval Operations during the Second World War.

entities.name: Cuthbert Collingwood
entities.fact: Cuthbert Collingwood led one column of the British fleet at Trafalgar and took command of it after Nelson's death.

entities.name: David Beatty
entities.fact: David Beatty commanded the British battlecruisers at Jutland and later became First Sea Lord.

entities.name: Reinhard Scheer
entities.fact: Reinhard Scheer led the German High Seas Fleet at the Battle of Jutland in 1916.

entities.name: Jacky Fisher
entities.fact: Jacky Fisher was the First Sea Lord who drove the building of HMS Dreadnought in 1906 and modernised the Royal Navy.

entities.name: George Anson
entities.fact: George Anson led a British circumnavigation of the globe from 1740 to 1744 and later reformed the Royal Navy.

entities.name: Edward Hawke
entities.fact: Edward Hawke destroyed a French fleet at the Battle of Quiberon Bay in 1759 during a gale.

entities.name: George Rodney
entities.fact: George Rodney won the Battle of the Saintes in 1782, breaking the French line in the Caribbean.

entities.name: Robert Blake
entities.fact: Robert Blake was a Commonwealth admiral who won victories against the Dutch and the Spanish in the 1650s.

entities.name: Michiel de Ruyter
entities.fact: Michiel de Ruyter was the Dutch admiral who led the daring raid up the River Medway in 1667.

entities.name: Maarten Tromp
entities.fact: Maarten Tromp was a Dutch admiral who destroyed a large Spanish fleet at the Battle of the Downs in 1639.

entities.name: Pierre-Charles Villeneuve
entities.fact: Pierre-Charles Villeneuve commanded the combined French and Spanish fleet defeated at Trafalgar in 1805.

entities.name: Marcus Agrippa
entities.fact: Marcus Agrippa was the admiral of Octavian who defeated Antony and Cleopatra at the Battle of Actium in 31 BC.

entities.name: John Jervis
entities.fact: John Jervis won the Battle of Cape St Vincent in 1797 and gave Nelson his first chance to shine.

entities.name: Richard Howe
entities.fact: Richard Howe won the Glorious First of June in 1794 and was known to his sailors as Black Dick.

entities.name: Fyodor Ushakov
entities.fact: Fyodor Ushakov was a Russian admiral who never lost a battle and who was later made a saint by the Russian Orthodox Church.

entities.name: Pavel Nakhimov
entities.fact: Pavel Nakhimov destroyed an Ottoman fleet at Sinop in 1853 and died defending Sevastopol in the Crimean War.

entities.name: Aleksandr Kolchak
entities.fact: Aleksandr Kolchak was a Russian admiral and polar explorer who led the anti-Bolshevik White forces in Siberia and was shot in 1920.

entities.name: Sergey Gorshkov
entities.fact: Sergey Gorshkov led the Soviet Navy from 1956 to 1985 and turned it into a global ocean-going force.

entities.name: Erich Raeder
entities.fact: Erich Raeder was the commander in chief of the German navy from 1928 until 1943.

entities.name: Gunther Lutjens
entities.fact: Gunther Lutjens commanded the German fleet in Operation Rheinubung and died when the Bismarck sank in 1941.

entities.name: Bertram Ramsay
entities.fact: Bertram Ramsay planned the evacuation of Dunkirk in 1940 and later the naval side of the Normandy landings.

entities.name: Andrew Cunningham
entities.fact: Andrew Cunningham led the Mediterranean Fleet in the Second World War and won the Battle of Cape Matapan in 1941.

entities.name: Louis Mountbatten
entities.fact: Louis Mountbatten was an Admiral of the Fleet and the last Viceroy of India, and he was killed by an IRA bomb in 1979.

entities.name: Chuichi Nagumo
entities.fact: Chuichi Nagumo led the Japanese carrier force that struck Pearl Harbor and that lost four carriers at Midway.

entities.name: Marc Mitscher
entities.fact: Marc Mitscher led the American fast carrier task force in the Pacific in the Second World War.

entities.name: Matthew Perry
entities.fact: Commodore Matthew Perry led a United States naval squadron into Tokyo Bay in 1853, pressing Japan to open its ports.

entities.name: Andrea Doria (admiral)
entities.fact: Andrea Doria was a Genoese admiral of the sixteenth century who ruled the seas for Genoa and served Emperor Charles V.

entities.name: Alvaro de Bazan
entities.fact: Alvaro de Bazan, Marquis of Santa Cruz, helped win Lepanto and was to lead the Spanish Armada but died in 1588 before it sailed.

entities.name: Maximilian von Spee
entities.fact: Maximilian von Spee commanded the German East Asia Squadron and died when it was destroyed at the Falkland Islands in 1914.

entities.name: Thomas Cochrane
entities.fact: Thomas Cochrane commanded the Chilean, Brazilian and Greek navies as well as the Royal Navy, and he is said to be a model for fictional heroes like Hornblower.

entities.name: Battle of Trafalgar
entities.fact: At Trafalgar in 1805 Nelson's fleet destroyed a larger French and Spanish force off the coast of Spain, though Nelson himself was killed.

entities.name: Battle of Midway
entities.fact: At Midway in June 1942 American aircraft sank four Japanese aircraft carriers, a turning point in the Pacific War.

entities.name: Battle of Jutland
entities.fact: Jutland in 1916 was the largest naval battle of the First World War, between the British Grand Fleet and the German High Seas Fleet.

entities.name: Spanish Armada
entities.fact: The Spanish Armada of 1588 was scattered by English fireships, gunnery at Gravelines and storms as it tried to invade England.

entities.name: Battle of the Atlantic
entities.fact: The Battle of the Atlantic from 1939 to 1945 was the longest continuous campaign of the Second World War, fought over Allied shipping against German U-boats.

entities.name: Battle of Salamis
entities.fact: At Salamis in 480 BC a smaller Greek fleet lured the Persians into a narrow strait and won a decisive victory.

entities.name: Battle of Lepanto
entities.fact: Lepanto in 1571, in which the Holy League beat the Ottoman fleet, was one of the last great battles fought mainly by oared galleys.

entities.name: Battle of Actium
entities.fact: At Actium in 31 BC Octavian's fleet defeated Mark Antony and Cleopatra, clearing his way to become the first Roman emperor.

entities.name: Battle of the Nile
entities.fact: At the Nile in 1798 Nelson destroyed most of the French fleet in Aboukir Bay, and the French flagship L'Orient blew up.

entities.name: Battle of Copenhagen
entities.fact: At Copenhagen in 1801 Nelson is said to have raised his telescope to his blind eye to ignore a signal to retreat.

entities.name: Battle of Leyte Gulf
entities.fact: Leyte Gulf in October 1944 is often described as the largest naval battle in history, fought around the Philippines.

entities.name: Battle of the Coral Sea
entities.fact: The Coral Sea in May 1942 was the first naval battle fought entirely by aircraft, with the opposing ships never in sight of each other.

entities.name: Battle of the River Plate
entities.fact: At the River Plate in December 1939 three British cruisers damaged the German pocket battleship Admiral Graf Spee, which was then scuttled off Montevideo.

entities.name: Battle of Tsushima
entities.fact: At Tsushima in May 1905 Admiral Togo's Japanese fleet destroyed the Russian Baltic Fleet after its long voyage around the world.

entities.name: Battle of Hampton Roads
entities.fact: Hampton Roads in March 1862 saw the first duel between ironclad warships, USS Monitor against CSS Virginia.

entities.name: Battle of the Philippine Sea
entities.fact: The Philippine Sea in June 1944 became known as the Great Marianas Turkey Shoot because American pilots shot down hundreds of Japanese aircraft.

entities.name: Battle of the Denmark Strait
entities.fact: In the Denmark Strait in May 1941 the German battleship Bismarck sank HMS Hood, leaving only three survivors.

entities.name: Battle of Taranto
entities.fact: At Taranto in November 1940 British Swordfish torpedo planes from the carrier Illustrious crippled the Italian battle fleet in harbour.

entities.name: Battle of the North Cape
entities.fact: At the North Cape in December 1943 a British force that included the battleship Duke of York sank the German battleship Scharnhorst.

entities.name: Battle of Quiberon Bay
entities.fact: At Quiberon Bay in 1759 Admiral Hawke chased the French fleet onto a rocky coast in a gale and wrecked its invasion plans.

entities.name: Battle of the Saintes
entities.fact: At the Saintes in 1782 Admiral Rodney's fleet broke the French line in the Caribbean and defeated Admiral de Grasse.

entities.name: Battle of Camperdown
entities.fact: Camperdown in 1797 was a British victory over the Dutch fleet off the Netherlands under Admiral Duncan.

entities.name: Glorious First of June
aliases: Battle of the Glorious First of June
entities.fact: The Glorious First of June in 1794 was fought to stop a French grain convoy from America reaching France.

entities.name: Battle of Navarino
entities.fact: Navarino in 1827 saw British, French and Russian ships destroy an Ottoman and Egyptian fleet, and it was the last major battle fought between sailing fleets.

entities.name: Battle of Manila Bay
entities.fact: At Manila Bay in May 1898 Commodore Dewey destroyed the Spanish Pacific squadron with very few American casualties.

entities.name: Battle of Lissa
entities.fact: At Lissa in 1866 the Austrian fleet under Tegetthoff rammed and sank Italian ironclads in a famous clash of early armoured ships.

entities.name: Battle of Sluys
entities.fact: At Sluys in 1340 Edward III's English fleet destroyed a French fleet in the early years of the Hundred Years' War.

entities.name: Battle of Lake Erie
entities.fact: At Lake Erie in 1813 Oliver Hazard Perry's American squadron captured a whole British fleet, and he reported that the enemy was ours.

entities.name: Battle of the Falkland Islands
entities.fact: At the Falkland Islands in December 1914 a British squadron destroyed Admiral von Spee's German East Asia Squadron.

entities.name: Battle of Coronel
entities.fact: At Coronel off Chile in November 1914 von Spee's squadron sank two British cruisers, the Royal Navy's first defeat in a fleet action for over a century.

entities.name: Battle of Cape Matapan
entities.fact: At Cape Matapan in March 1941 Admiral Cunningham's fleet sank three Italian heavy cruisers off southern Greece.

entities.name: Battle of Savo Island
entities.fact: At Savo Island in August 1942 a Japanese night attack sank four Allied heavy cruisers in one of the worst American naval defeats.

entities.name: Battle of Cape St Vincent
entities.fact: At Cape St Vincent in 1797 Commodore Nelson left the line without orders to capture two Spanish ships and helped win the battle.

entities.name: Battle of Dogger Bank (1915)
entities.fact: At Dogger Bank in January 1915 British battlecruisers sank the German armoured cruiser Blucher in the North Sea.

entities.name: Battle of Heligoland Bight
entities.fact: Heligoland Bight in August 1914 was the first major naval action of the First World War, and the British sank three German cruisers.

entities.name: Battle of the Bismarck Sea
entities.fact: In the Bismarck Sea in March 1943 Allied aircraft sank most of a Japanese troop convoy heading for New Guinea.

entities.name: Battle of the Barents Sea
entities.fact: The Barents Sea battle of December 1942 saw British destroyers drive off larger German warships attacking an Arctic convoy, which enraged Hitler.

entities.name: Battle of Sinop
entities.fact: At Sinop in 1853 a Russian squadron destroyed an Ottoman fleet in harbour, helping bring Britain and France into the Crimean War.

entities.name: Battle of the Yalu River
entities.fact: At the Yalu River in 1894 the Japanese fleet defeated the Chinese Beiyang Fleet in the first big clash of modern steam warships.

entities.name: Battle of Chesma
entities.fact: At Chesma in 1770 the Russian fleet used fireships to burn the Ottoman fleet in a Turkish bay.

entities.name: Battle of Mylae
entities.fact: At Mylae in 260 BC the Romans beat Carthage using boarding bridges called corvus, their first major naval victory.

entities.name: Battle of the Aegates Islands
entities.fact: The Aegates Islands in 241 BC was the Roman naval victory over Carthage that ended the First Punic War.

entities.name: Battle of Arginusae
entities.fact: Arginusae in 406 BC was an Athenian naval victory, after which Athens controversially executed generals who failed to rescue survivors.

entities.name: Battle of Aegospotami
entities.fact: At Aegospotami in 405 BC the Spartan Lysander destroyed the Athenian fleet, effectively ending the Peloponnesian War.

entities.name: Battle of La Hogue
entities.fact: La Hogue in 1692 saw the Anglo-Dutch fleet destroy French ships that were meant to cover an invasion of England.

entities.name: Battle of Beachy Head
entities.fact: Beachy Head in 1690 was a French victory over a combined English and Dutch fleet in the English Channel.

entities.name: Battle of Texel
entities.fact: Texel in 1673 was the last battle of the Third Anglo-Dutch War, in which de Ruyter prevented an Anglo-French landing in the Netherlands.

entities.name: Battle of Lowestoft
entities.fact: Lowestoft in 1665 was a major English victory over the Dutch in the Second Anglo-Dutch War.

entities.name: Battle of Solebay
entities.fact: At Solebay in 1672 de Ruyter surprised the Anglo-French fleet at anchor off the Suffolk coast.

entities.name: Battle of Gangut
entities.fact: Gangut in 1714 was the first major Russian naval victory, won over the Swedes in the Baltic with Peter the Great taking part.

entities.name: Battle of Dan-no-ura
entities.fact: At Dan-no-ura in 1185 the Minamoto destroyed the Taira fleet in the Shimonoseki Strait, and the child emperor Antoku drowned.

entities.name: Battleship
entities.fact: Battleships were heavily armoured warships with the biggest guns afloat, and the last ones were retired by the early 1990s.

entities.name: Destroyer
entities.fact: Destroyers are fast, manoeuvrable warships, first built in the 1890s to destroy torpedo boats and now used to escort fleets and hunt submarines.

entities.name: Aircraft carrier
entities.fact: An aircraft carrier is a warship with a long flight deck that serves as a floating airbase for the fleet's aircraft.

entities.name: Frigate
entities.fact: Frigates were fast sailing warships in Nelson's day, and the name now describes a modern escort warship smaller than a destroyer.

entities.name: Cruiser
entities.fact: Cruisers are large, fast warships that traditionally scouted for fleets, protected trade routes and raided enemy shipping.

entities.name: Ship of the line
entities.fact: Ships of the line were the biggest sailing warships, built to fight in a single line with rows of cannon along their sides.

entities.name: Dreadnought
entities.fact: The dreadnought was a type of battleship named after HMS Dreadnought of 1906, which carried a single large calibre of main gun and made earlier battleships obsolete.

entities.name: Corvette
entities.fact: Corvettes are the smallest class of warship that is still regarded as an ocean-going combatant, and hundreds were built to escort convoys in the Second World War.

entities.name: Battlecruiser
entities.fact: Battlecruisers had the guns of a battleship but thinner armour in exchange for greater speed, and three exploded at Jutland.

entities.name: Minesweeper
entities.fact: Minesweepers clear sea mines and are often built with wooden or plastic hulls so that magnetic mines do not detect them.

entities.name: Ironclad
entities.fact: Ironclads were steam warships protected by iron armour plates, and they appeared in the 1850s and 1860s.

entities.name: Gunboat
entities.fact: A gunboat is a small armed vessel built to carry heavy guns, and it was used for centuries to patrol rivers and coasts.

entities.name: Man-of-war
entities.fact: A man-of-war was a large armed sailing ship of a navy, from which the name for the jellyfish-like Portuguese man o' war was borrowed.

entities.name: Sloop-of-war
entities.fact: A sloop-of-war was a small sailing warship with guns on one deck, and it was used for patrol and escort duty.

entities.name: Patrol boat
entities.fact: Patrol boats are small, fast naval or coastguard vessels used to guard coasts, harbours and rivers.

entities.name: Amphibious assault ship
entities.fact: An amphibious assault ship carries troops, landing craft and helicopters so a force can be put ashore from the sea.

entities.name: Pre-dreadnought
entities.fact: Pre-dreadnoughts were the steel battleships built before HMS Dreadnought in 1906, with a mix of heavy and medium guns.

entities.name: Monitor
entities.fact: Monitors were low-freeboard warships with a few big guns, named for USS Monitor of 1862, and they were used for shore bombardment.

entities.name: Fire ship
entities.fact: A fire ship was an old vessel packed with flammables, set alight and sailed into an enemy fleet, as at Gravelines in 1588.

entities.name: Bireme
entities.fact: The bireme was an ancient oared warship with two banks of oars on each side, often fitted with a bronze ram.

entities.name: Quinquereme
entities.fact: The quinquereme was the standard large warship of Carthage and Rome in the Punic Wars, rowed by crews of several hundred.

entities.name: Q-ship
entities.fact: A Q-ship was a heavily armed warship disguised as a harmless merchant vessel to lure submarines into surface attack.

entities.name: Torpedo boat
entities.fact: Torpedo boats were small, fast craft armed with torpedoes, built in the late nineteenth century to threaten much larger warships.

entities.name: Destroyer escort
entities.fact: The destroyer escort was a smaller, cheaper warship type built by the United States in the Second World War to guard convoys against submarines.

entities.name: Escort carrier
entities.fact: Escort carriers were small, slower aircraft carriers built on merchant hulls to protect convoys in the Second World War.

entities.name: Light cruiser
entities.fact: A light cruiser was a cruiser with lighter armour and guns than a heavy cruiser, mainly used for scouting and leading destroyers.

entities.name: Heavy cruiser
entities.fact: A heavy cruiser was defined by the 1922 Washington Naval Treaty as a cruiser with guns of more than six inches.

entities.name: Armoured cruiser
entities.fact: Armoured cruisers were cruisers with side armour like a battleship's, and they were built in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries.

entities.name: Bomb vessel
entities.fact: A bomb vessel was a heavily built sailing ship carrying mortars to shell coastal forts and towns from the sea.

entities.name: Missile boat
entities.fact: Missile boats are small, fast craft carrying anti-ship missiles, first used to dramatic effect when Egyptian-launched missiles sank the Israeli destroyer Eilat in 1967.

entities.name: Helicopter carrier
entities.fact: A helicopter carrier is a ship designed to operate helicopters from its deck, and many are also used to land troops.

entities.name: Dromon
entities.fact: The dromon was the main warship of the Byzantine navy, an oared ship used to hurl Greek fire at enemy vessels.

entities.name: Penteconter
entities.fact: The penteconter was an early Greek warship rowed by fifty oarsmen in a single bank on each side.

entities.name: Liburna
entities.fact: The liburna was a light, fast Roman warship modelled on the vessels of the Liburnian pirates of the Adriatic.

entities.name: Xebec
entities.fact: The xebec was a lateen-rigged Mediterranean ship used by Barbary corsairs and by European navies.

entities.name: Galleass
entities.fact: A galleass was a larger and more heavily armed version of the galley, with guns along the bow, and six of them played a major part at Lepanto in 1571.

entities.name: Razee
entities.fact: A razee was a warship that had one deck cut away, converting a ship of the line into a faster frigate-like vessel.

entities.name: Coastal defence ship
entities.fact: A coastal defence ship was a small battleship built mainly to protect a nation's own coasts, and Scandinavian navies built many.

entities.name: Motor torpedo boat
entities.fact: Motor torpedo boats were small, fast, wooden or light-alloy craft that attacked larger ships with torpedoes in the Second World War.

entities.name: Minelayer
entities.fact: A minelayer is a ship built to lay sea mines in advance of an enemy fleet or to defend a harbour.

entities.name: Seaplane tender
entities.fact: A seaplane tender was a ship that supported seaplanes, carrying and servicing them at sea, and the first aircraft carriers grew from them.

entities.name: Auxiliary cruiser
entities.fact: An auxiliary cruiser was a merchant ship converted to carry guns for raiding or patrolling, a common German tactic in both world wars.

entities.name: Littoral combat ship
entities.fact: The littoral combat ship is a modern, fast American warship class designed to operate in shallow coastal waters.

entities.name: Guided missile cruiser
entities.fact: A guided missile cruiser is a modern large warship built around missile systems for air defence and attack, such as the American Ticonderoga class.

entities.name: Ballistic missile submarine
entities.fact: A ballistic missile submarine is a nuclear-powered vessel that carries long-range nuclear missiles and is meant to stay hidden at sea.

entities.name: Fast battleship
entities.fact: Fast battleships, such as the American Iowa class of the Second World War, combined heavy guns with speeds of over thirty knots.

entities.name: Pocket battleship
entities.fact: Pocket battleship was the British nickname for Germany's Deutschland class of the 1930s, which packed heavy guns into a hull limited by the Treaty of Versailles.

entities.name: Yellow Submarine
entities.fact: The Yellow Submarine is the fictional vessel of the 1966 Beatles song and the 1968 animated film of the same name.

entities.name: Nautilus
entities.fact: The Nautilus is Captain Nemo's fictional electric-powered submarine in Jules Verne's 1870 novel Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Seas.

entities.name: USS Nautilus
entities.fact: USS Nautilus, launched in 1954, was the world's first nuclear-powered submarine and in 1958 made the first submerged crossing of the North Pole.

entities.name: Titan
entities.fact: Titan was a privately owned submersible that imploded in June 2023 during a dive to the wreck of the Titanic, killing all five people aboard.

entities.name: Turtle
entities.fact: The Turtle was a one-man, hand-cranked submersible built by David Bushnell that tried to attach a bomb to a British warship in New York harbour in 1776.

entities.name: Red October
entities.fact: The Red October is the fictional Soviet missile submarine in Tom Clancy's 1984 novel The Hunt for Red October.

entities.name: U-505
entities.fact: U-505 was a German submarine captured intact by the United States Navy in June 1944 and is now displayed at the Museum of Science and Industry in Chicago.

entities.name: K-19
entities.fact: K-19 was a Soviet nuclear submarine whose reactor coolant system failed in 1961, earning it the nickname Hiroshima and inspiring a 2002 film.

entities.name: HMS Conqueror
entities.fact: HMS Conqueror sank the Argentine cruiser General Belgrano in 1982, the only time a nuclear-powered submarine has sunk a ship in wartime.

entities.name: Surcouf
entities.fact: Surcouf was a giant French submarine of 1929 that carried a seaplane in a hangar, and she was lost in the Caribbean in 1942.

entities.name: USS Skate
entities.fact: USS Skate was the first submarine to surface at the North Pole, which she did in March 1959.

entities.name: USS Triton
entities.fact: USS Triton was an American nuclear submarine that made the first submerged circumnavigation of the globe in 1960.

entities.name: USS Holland
entities.fact: USS Holland was the first submarine commissioned by the United States Navy, in 1900, and was designed by the Irish inventor John Philip Holland.

entities.name: I-400
entities.fact: The Japanese I-400 submarines were the largest built before nuclear boats, and each carried three folding seaplanes in a hangar.

entities.name: Pisces III
entities.fact: Pisces III was a British submersible that sank off Ireland in 1973 and whose two crew were rescued after about three days on the seabed.

entities.name: Resurgam
entities.fact: Resurgam was a steam-powered submarine built by the Reverend George Garrett in 1879, and it sank under tow off Wales in 1880.

entities.name: Ictineo II
entities.fact: Ictineo II was an early Spanish submarine designed by Narcis Monturiol and launched in 1864.

entities.name: Peral
entities.fact: The Peral was an electric-powered Spanish submarine built by Isaac Peral and launched in 1888.

entities.name: Gymnote
entities.fact: The Gymnote was an experimental electric submarine launched in France in 1888.

entities.name: HMS Thetis
entities.fact: HMS Thetis sank in Liverpool Bay during trials in 1939 with the loss of 99 lives, was raised and later served as HMS Thunderbolt.

entities.name: HMS Affray
entities.fact: HMS Affray was lost in the English Channel in 1951 with all 75 men aboard, the last Royal Navy submarine lost at sea.

entities.name: Aluminaut
entities.fact: Aluminaut was a research submarine built with an aluminium hull in 1964 that helped search for a lost hydrogen bomb off Spain in 1966.

entities.name: Johnson Sea Link
entities.fact: The Johnson Sea Link was a research submersible, and two men died in 1973 when it became entangled in a wreck off Key West.

entities.name: Denise
entities.fact: Denise was Jacques Cousteau's nickname for his SP-350 diving saucer, a small two-person submersible built in 1959.

entities.name: Seehund
entities.fact: The Seehund was a German two-man midget submarine of the Second World War, built in large numbers in 1944 and 1945.

entities.name: HMS Holland 1
entities.fact: HMS Holland 1 was the Royal Navy's first submarine, launched in 1901, and it is now preserved at the Royal Navy Submarine Museum.

entities.name: Brandtaucher
entities.fact: The Brandtaucher was a German submarine built by Wilhelm Bauer that sank in Kiel harbour in 1851, and its three crew escaped by flooding the vessel.

entities.name: RMS Queen Mary
entities.fact: The Queen Mary was a Cunard liner launched in 1934 that now serves as a hotel and museum in Long Beach, California.

entities.name: Queen Elizabeth 2
entities.fact: Queen Elizabeth 2 sailed for Cunard from 1969 to 2008 and has since become a floating hotel in Dubai.

entities.name: RMS Olympic
entities.fact: The Olympic was the Titanic's older sister ship, and she served for twenty-four years from 1911 to 1935.

entities.name: Queen Mary 2
entities.fact: The Queen Mary 2 entered service in 2004 and is a Cunard ocean liner still running regular transatlantic crossings.

entities.name: SS Normandie
entities.fact: The Normandie was a lavish art-deco French liner of 1935 that caught fire and capsized at her New York pier in 1942.

entities.name: SS United States
entities.fact: The SS United States won the Blue Riband for the fastest Atlantic crossing on her maiden voyage in 1952.

entities.name: RMS Mauretania
entities.fact: The Mauretania was a Cunard liner of 1907 that held the Blue Riband for fastest Atlantic crossing for about two decades.

entities.name: RMS Aquitania
entities.fact: The Aquitania was a Cunard liner launched in 1913 that served in two world wars and sailed for around thirty-five years.

entities.name: SS Great Eastern
entities.fact: The Great Eastern was Isambard Brunel's enormous iron ship, which in 1866 laid a lasting transatlantic telegraph cable.

entities.name: SS Great Britain
entities.fact: The SS Great Britain, launched in 1843 by Brunel, was the first iron-hulled, propeller-driven ship to cross the Atlantic and is preserved in Bristol.

entities.name: Oasis of the Seas
entities.fact: Oasis of the Seas, which entered service in 2009, was the world's largest passenger ship when she was built.

entities.name: RMS Queen Elizabeth
entities.fact: The Queen Elizabeth was the largest passenger liner in the world when she entered service in 1940, and she burned in Hong Kong harbour in 1972.

entities.name: Diamond Princess
entities.fact: The Diamond Princess was quarantined at Yokohama in February 2020 after a COVID-19 outbreak among her passengers.

entities.name: RMS Empress of Ireland
entities.fact: The Empress of Ireland sank in the Saint Lawrence River in 1914 after a collision, with the loss of over 1,000 lives.

entities.name: Icon of the Seas
entities.fact: Icon of the Seas entered service in 2024 as the world's largest cruise ship by gross tonnage.

entities.name: Wonder of the Seas
entities.fact: Wonder of the Seas entered service in 2022 as the largest cruise ship in the world at the time.

entities.name: Allure of the Seas
entities.fact: Allure of the Seas is the 2010 sister ship of Oasis of the Seas, with a central park of real trees running through the ship.

entities.name: Harmony of the Seas
entities.fact: Harmony of the Seas, which entered service in 2016, is the third of Royal Caribbean's Oasis-class cruise ships.

entities.name: Symphony of the Seas
entities.fact: Symphony of the Seas, built in 2018, is a Royal Caribbean cruise ship of the Oasis class.

entities.name: Morro Castle
entities.fact: The Morro Castle was an American liner that caught fire off New Jersey in 1934, killing 137 people.

entities.name: SS France
entities.fact: The SS France of 1962 was the longest passenger ship in the world for decades, and she later sailed as the cruise ship Norway.

entities.name: Achille Lauro
entities.fact: The Achille Lauro was an Italian cruise ship hijacked by terrorists in 1985, and she sank in 1994 after a fire.

entities.name: Carnival Triumph
entities.fact: The Carnival Triumph was crippled by an engine-room fire in 2013 and drifted for days in the Gulf of Mexico, with passengers left without power.

entities.name: Ruby Princess
entities.fact: The Ruby Princess was a cruise ship whose passengers disembarked in Sydney in March 2020, and COVID-19 cases were later traced to the voyage.

entities.name: SS Rex
entities.fact: The Rex was an Italian liner that won the Blue Riband in 1933.

entities.name: SS Bremen
entities.fact: The Bremen was a German liner that took the Blue Riband for the fastest Atlantic crossing in 1929.

entities.name: SS Vaterland
entities.fact: The Vaterland was a giant German liner of 1914 that was seized by the United States in 1917 and renamed Leviathan.

entities.name: SS Imperator
entities.fact: The Imperator of 1913 was the largest ship in the world when launched, and she later became Cunard's Berengaria.

entities.name: Kaiser Wilhelm der Grosse
entities.fact: Kaiser Wilhelm der Grosse of 1897 was the first liner with four funnels and won the Blue Riband.

entities.name: RMS Majestic
entities.fact: The Majestic was launched in Germany as the Bismarck and completed for White Star in 1922, and she was the largest ship in the world until 1935.

entities.name: Conte di Savoia
entities.fact: The Conte di Savoia was an Italian liner of 1932 fitted with huge gyroscopes to reduce rolling.

entities.name: MS Stockholm
entities.fact: The Stockholm was the Swedish liner whose bow collided with the Andrea Doria off Nantucket in 1956.

entities.name: SS Savannah
entities.fact: The Savannah, in 1819, was the first steam-powered vessel to cross the Atlantic, though she sailed for most of the voyage.

entities.name: SS Canberra
entities.fact: The P&O liner Canberra was requisitioned as a troopship during the Falklands War of 1982.

entities.name: MS Prinsendam
entities.fact: The Prinsendam caught fire in the Gulf of Alaska in 1980, and all 520 people aboard were rescued before she sank.

entities.name: SS Arctic
entities.fact: The American paddle steamer Arctic sank in 1854 after colliding with another ship off Newfoundland, and about 350 people died.

entities.name: Pacific Princess
entities.fact: The Pacific Princess was the cruise ship featured in the television series The Love Boat, and the programme's opening credits showed her.

entities.name: RMS Britannia
entities.fact: The Britannia was the first Cunard steamship on the Atlantic route in 1840, and she carried Charles Dickens to America in 1842.

entities.name: SS Atlantic
entities.fact: The White Star liner Atlantic struck rocks off Nova Scotia in 1873, and more than 500 people died.

entities.name: SS Waratah
entities.fact: The Waratah, an Australian liner, vanished off South Africa in 1909 with 211 people on board, and no wreck has been confirmed.

entities.name: Columbus's first voyage
entities.fact: On his first voyage in 1492 Christopher Columbus sailed with the Santa Maria, Nina and Pinta and made landfall in the Bahamas.

entities.name: Mayflower voyage
entities.fact: The Mayflower carried about 100 passengers from Plymouth, England, in 1620 and reached Cape Cod after crossing the Atlantic.

entities.name: Kon-Tiki expedition
entities.fact: In 1947 Thor Heyerdahl and five companions sailed a balsa raft from Peru across the Pacific to the Tuamotu islands.

entities.name: Voyage of the Beagle
entities.fact: The Voyage of the Beagle from 1831 to 1836 carried the young Charles Darwin around the world and shaped his later ideas on evolution.

entities.name: Magellan's circumnavigation
entities.fact: Magellan's expedition of 1519 to 1522 was the first to sail around the world, though Magellan died in the Philippines and only one of five ships returned.

entities.name: Endurance expedition
entities.fact: Shackleton's Endurance expedition of 1914 to 1917 lost its ship to the Weddell Sea ice yet every man of the party survived.

entities.name: Challenger expedition
entities.fact: The Challenger expedition of 1872 to 1876 was the first major scientific survey of the world's oceans, and it sounded the Mariana Trench.

entities.name: Cook's first voyage
entities.fact: On his first voyage of 1768 to 1771 in the Endeavour, James Cook observed the transit of Venus at Tahiti and charted New Zealand and Australia's east coast.

entities.name: Vasco da Gama's voyage to India
entities.fact: Vasco da Gama's voyage of 1497 to 1499 was the first sea route from Europe to India, reaching Calicut in 1498.

entities.name: Bartolomeu Dias's voyage
aliases: Dias rounds the Cape of Good Hope
entities.fact: In 1488 Bartolomeu Dias became the first European known to round the southern tip of Africa.

entities.name: John Cabot's voyage
entities.fact: John Cabot sailed from Bristol in the Matthew in 1497 and reached the coast of North America.

entities.name: Zheng He's treasure voyages
entities.fact: Between 1405 and 1433 Zheng He led seven huge Chinese treasure fleets across the Indian Ocean as far as East Africa.

entities.name: Franklin's lost expedition
entities.fact: Sir John Franklin's expedition of 1845 to find the Northwest Passage vanished with HMS Erebus, HMS Terror and all 129 men.

entities.name: Fram expedition
entities.fact: Fridtjof Nansen's Fram expedition of 1893 to 1896 deliberately froze the ship into Arctic ice to drift towards the North Pole.

entities.name: Discovery expedition
entities.fact: The Discovery expedition of 1901 to 1904 was Robert Falcon Scott's first Antarctic expedition, aboard the ship RRS Discovery.

entities.name: Terra Nova expedition
entities.fact: The Terra Nova expedition of 1910 to 1913 reached the South Pole, but Scott and his four companions died on the return march.

entities.name: Golden Globe Race
entities.fact: The 1968 Golden Globe Race was the first solo non-stop round-the-world yacht race, and Robin Knox-Johnston was the only finisher.

entities.name: Joshua Slocum's solo circumnavigation
entities.fact: Joshua Slocum sailed alone around the world in his sloop Spray from 1895 to 1898, the first person to do so.

entities.name: Gjoa expedition
entities.fact: Roald Amundsen's Gjoa expedition of 1903 to 1906 was the first to navigate the Northwest Passage by ship.

entities.name: Drake's circumnavigation
entities.fact: Francis Drake sailed round the world from 1577 to 1580 in the Golden Hind and was knighted for it by Elizabeth I.

entities.name: Anson's circumnavigation
entities.fact: George Anson's voyage of 1740 to 1744 captured a Spanish treasure galleon and returned with only a fraction of his original crews.

entities.name: Bligh's open boat voyage
entities.fact: After the mutiny on the Bounty in 1789, William Bligh and eighteen loyalists sailed a small open boat about 3,600 nautical miles to Timor.

entities.name: Tasman's voyage of 1642
entities.fact: Abel Tasman's 1642 voyage was the first European sighting of Tasmania and New Zealand.

entities.name: Henry Hudson's last voyage
entities.fact: In 1610 Henry Hudson sailed into what is now Hudson Bay, and after a mutiny in 1611 his crew set him adrift in a small boat.

entities.name: Belgica expedition
entities.fact: The Belgica expedition of 1897 to 1899 was the first to winter in the Antarctic, when its ship became trapped in ice.

entities.name: Nimrod expedition
entities.fact: On the Nimrod expedition of 1907 to 1909 Ernest Shackleton's party turned back only about 97 nautical miles short of the South Pole.

entities.name: Jeannette expedition
entities.fact: The Jeannette expedition of 1879 to 1881 was an American Arctic voyage that ended when the ship was crushed by ice and most of the crew died.

entities.name: Vega expedition
entities.fact: The Vega expedition of 1878 to 1880, led by Adolf Nordenskiold, was the first to sail the Northeast Passage along Siberia's coast.

entities.name: La Perouse expedition
entities.fact: The French expedition of La Perouse left in 1785 and vanished in the Pacific, and its wrecks were found at Vanikoro in the following century.

entities.name: Brendan Voyage
entities.fact: In 1976 and 1977 Tim Severin sailed a leather-hulled boat from Ireland to Newfoundland to show that the legendary voyage of Saint Brendan was possible.

entities.name: Hokule'a voyage to Tahiti
entities.fact: In 1976 the double-hulled canoe Hokule'a sailed from Hawaii to Tahiti using traditional navigation without instruments.

entities.name: Great Northern Expedition
entities.fact: The Great Northern Expedition of 1733 to 1743 was a huge Russian effort that mapped Siberia's Arctic coast and took Vitus Bering to Alaska.

entities.name: Ra expeditions
entities.fact: On the Ra expeditions of 1969 and 1970 Thor Heyerdahl sailed papyrus reed boats across the Atlantic, and Ra II reached Barbados.

entities.name: Tigris expedition
entities.fact: In 1977 and 1978 Thor Heyerdahl's reed boat Tigris sailed from Iraq to Djibouti, where he burned it in protest of regional wars.

entities.name: Malaspina expedition
entities.fact: The Malaspina expedition of 1789 to 1794 was a Spanish scientific voyage around the Americas and the Pacific.

entities.name: Sea Venture voyage
entities.fact: The Sea Venture was wrecked on Bermuda in 1609 while sailing to Jamestown, and the story may have inspired Shakespeare's The Tempest.

entities.name: Leif Eriksson's voyage to Vinland
entities.fact: Around the year 1000 the Norse explorer Leif Eriksson sailed to North America from Greenland and named it Vinland.

entities.name: Barentsz's voyages
entities.fact: Willem Barentsz led Dutch Arctic expeditions in the 1590s, and his crew survived the winter of 1596 and 1597 on Novaya Zemlya.

entities.name: Cabral's voyage
entities.fact: In 1500 Pedro Alvares Cabral's fleet, bound for India, landed in Brazil and claimed it for Portugal.

entities.name: Pytheas's voyage
entities.fact: Around 325 BC the Greek explorer Pytheas sailed from Massalia to northern Europe and described a distant land he called Thule.

entities.name: Hanno's voyage
entities.fact: The Carthaginian Hanno led a fleet down the west coast of Africa, and a Greek version of his account survives as the Periplus of Hanno.

entities.name: Nearchus's voyage
entities.fact: In 325 to 324 BC Alexander the Great's admiral Nearchus led a fleet from the Indus River to the Persian Gulf.

entities.name: Mary Celeste
entities.fact: The Mary Celeste was found drifting and abandoned in the Atlantic in 1872, and her crew and passengers were never found.

entities.name: Tara Oceans expedition
entities.fact: The Tara Oceans expedition of 2009 to 2013 sailed the schooner Tara around the world to sample plankton.

entities.name: Harbo and Samuelsen's Atlantic row
entities.fact: In 1896 George Harbo and Frank Samuelsen became the first people to row across the Atlantic, from New York to the Isles of Scilly, in about 55 days.

entities.name: Ellen MacArthur's record voyage
entities.fact: In 2005 Ellen MacArthur broke the record for the fastest solo non-stop circumnavigation of the globe, in about 71 days.

entities.name: Vendee Globe
entities.fact: The Vendee Globe is a solo, non-stop, unassisted round-the-world yacht race held every four years since 1989.

entities.name: Wilkes expedition
entities.fact: The Wilkes expedition of 1838 to 1842 was a United States naval survey that charted a long stretch of the Antarctic coast.

entities.name: Ross Antarctic expedition
entities.fact: The Ross expedition of 1839 to 1843 sailed HMS Erebus and HMS Terror to discover the Ross Sea and the Ross Ice Shelf.

entities.name: Hatshepsut's expedition to Punt
entities.fact: Around 1470 BC the Egyptian queen Hatshepsut sent a fleet to Punt, and the voyage is shown in carvings at her temple at Deir el-Bahari.

entities.name: Fish and chips
entities.fact: Fish and chips is the classic British takeaway of battered fish with fried potatoes, and it has been sold in England since the 1860s.

entities.name: Sushi
entities.fact: Sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice served with raw or cooked fish and other toppings.

entities.name: Clam chowder
entities.fact: Clam chowder is a thick soup of clams and potatoes, creamy in New England and tomato-based in the Manhattan version.

entities.name: Paella
entities.fact: Paella is a rice dish from Valencia in Spain, cooked in a wide shallow pan, and the seafood version is known across the world.

entities.name: Fried calamari
entities.fact: Fried calamari is squid cut into rings, battered or breaded and deep-fried, and it is served all over the Mediterranean.

entities.name: Sashimi
entities.fact: Sashimi is thin slices of very fresh raw fish or seafood, served without rice in Japanese cooking.

entities.name: Ceviche
entities.fact: Ceviche is raw fish cured in lime or lemon juice with onion and chilli, and it is a national dish of Peru.

entities.name: Bouillabaisse
entities.fact: Bouillabaisse is a fish stew from the port of Marseille, flavoured with saffron and traditionally made from local rockfish.

entities.name: Lobster roll
entities.fact: A lobster roll is a toasted bun filled with lobster meat, and it is a New England speciality.

entities.name: Crab cakes
entities.fact: Crab cakes are patties of crab meat, bound and fried or baked, and they are strongly associated with Maryland.

entities.name: Fish tacos
entities.fact: Fish tacos, which came out of Baja California in Mexico, use fried or grilled fish in a tortilla with cabbage and sauce.

entities.name: Prawn cocktail
entities.fact: Prawn cocktail is a starter of prawns in a pink sauce on lettuce, which was hugely popular in Britain in the 1960s and 1970s.

entities.name: Shrimp scampi
entities.fact: Shrimp scampi is shrimp cooked in garlic, butter and white wine, and the dish is an Italian-American adaptation named for langoustines.

entities.name: Moules marinieres
entities.fact: Moules marinieres is a French dish of mussels steamed in white wine with shallots and parsley.

entities.name: Kedgeree
entities.fact: Kedgeree is a dish of rice, smoked haddock and boiled eggs that British colonials adapted from the Indian dish khichdi.

entities.name: Fish pie
entities.fact: Fish pie is a British dish of fish in a creamy sauce under a mashed potato crust.

entities.name: Poke
entities.fact: Poke is a Hawaiian dish of cubed raw fish, usually tuna, seasoned with soy sauce and sesame oil.

entities.name: Tempura
entities.fact: Tempura is Japanese battered and deep-fried seafood or vegetables, a technique that Portuguese traders brought to Japan in the sixteenth century.

entities.name: Lobster thermidor
entities.fact: Lobster thermidor is a French dish of lobster meat in a creamy sauce, returned to its shell and browned under the grill.

entities.name: Cioppino
entities.fact: Cioppino is a tomato-based fish stew from San Francisco, created by Italian fishermen who settled there.

entities.name: Oysters Rockefeller
entities.fact: Oysters Rockefeller, created in New Orleans in 1899 at Antoine's restaurant, was named for the richness of its sauce.

entities.name: Tom yum goong
entities.fact: Tom yum goong is a hot and sour Thai soup with prawns, lemongrass, galangal and lime leaves.

entities.name: Fritto misto
entities.fact: Fritto misto is an Italian dish of mixed fried seafood, typically including small fish, squid and prawns.

entities.name: Zarzuela
entities.fact: Zarzuela is a Catalan stew of fish and shellfish in a tomato and almond-thickened sauce.

entities.name: Gravlax
entities.fact: Gravlax is a Nordic dish of salmon cured with salt, sugar and dill, and the name comes from words meaning buried salmon.

entities.name: Cullen skink
entities.fact: Cullen skink is a Scottish soup of smoked haddock, potatoes and onions from the town of Cullen in Moray.

entities.name: Stargazy pie
entities.fact: Stargazy pie is a Cornish pie in which whole pilchards poke their heads through the pastry crust, linked to the village of Mousehole.

entities.name: Chilli crab
entities.fact: Chilli crab is a Singaporean dish of mud crab in a sweet and spicy tomato and chilli sauce.

entities.name: Takoyaki
entities.fact: Takoyaki are Japanese balls of batter with a piece of octopus inside, a street food that comes from Osaka.

entities.name: Pulpo a la gallega
entities.fact: Pulpo a la gallega is boiled octopus served with olive oil, paprika and salt, a traditional dish of Galicia in Spain.

entities.name: Cacciucco
entities.fact: Cacciucco is a rich Tuscan fish stew from the port of Livorno, served over toasted bread.

entities.name: Brandade
entities.fact: Brandade is a creamy Provencal purée of salt cod with olive oil and garlic.

entities.name: Lobster Newburg
entities.fact: Lobster Newburg is an American dish of lobster in a sauce of cream, butter, egg yolks and sherry.

entities.name: Crab rangoon
entities.fact: Crab rangoon is a deep-fried dumpling filled with cream cheese and crab, found in American Chinese restaurants.

entities.name: Surstromming
entities.fact: Surstromming is a Swedish fermented Baltic herring, famous for the powerful smell that comes out of the tin when opened.

entities.name: Lutefisk
entities.fact: Lutefisk is dried whitefish rehydrated with lye and then boiled, a traditional Scandinavian Christmas dish.

entities.name: Jellied eels
entities.fact: Jellied eels are chopped eel set in cold jelly, a traditional dish of London's East End.

entities.name: Bacalhau a Bras
entities.fact: Bacalhau a Bras is a Portuguese dish of shredded salt cod, fried potato and scrambled egg.

entities.name: Fesikh
entities.fact: Fesikh is fermented, salted grey mullet eaten in Egypt at the spring festival of Sham el-Nessim.

entities.name: Kinilaw
entities.fact: Kinilaw is a Filipino dish of raw fish cured in vinegar with ginger, onion and chilli.

entities.name: Poisson cru
entities.fact: Poisson cru is the national dish of Tahiti, raw fish marinated in lime juice and finished with coconut milk.

entities.name: Amok trey
entities.fact: Amok trey is a Cambodian steamed fish curry in coconut milk and kroeung paste, traditionally served in banana leaves.

entities.name: Mohinga
entities.fact: Mohinga is a Burmese fish soup with rice noodles, often described as the national dish of Myanmar.

entities.name: Machher jhol
entities.fact: Machher jhol is a light, spiced Bengali fish curry, usually made with freshwater fish such as rohu.

entities.name: Moqueca
entities.fact: Moqueca is a Brazilian fish stew, made in the state of Bahia with coconut milk and palm oil and in Espirito Santo with tomato and annatto.

entities.name: Caldeirada
entities.fact: Caldeirada is a Portuguese fish stew of layered fish, potatoes, onions and tomatoes.

entities.name: Rakfisk
entities.fact: Rakfisk is Norwegian trout that is salted and fermented for months and eaten uncooked.

entities.name: Lohikeitto
entities.fact: Lohikeitto is a creamy Finnish salmon soup with potatoes and dill.

entities.name: Fugu
entities.fact: Fugu is Japanese pufferfish, which must be prepared by specially licensed chefs because its organs contain a deadly toxin.

entities.name: Kokoda
entities.fact: Kokoda is a Fijian dish of raw fish marinated in lime juice and served in coconut cream.

entities.name: Rollmops
entities.fact: Rollmops are pickled herring fillets rolled around a pickle or onion, a German and Scandinavian speciality.

entities.name: Hakarl
entities.fact: Hakarl is an Icelandic dish of Greenland shark, which is poisonous when fresh and is cured by fermenting and hanging to dry.

entities.name: Frying
entities.fact: Frying cooks fish in hot fat, as in the battered fillets of British fish and chips.

entities.name: Grilling
entities.fact: Grilling cooks fish over or under direct heat, and whole sardines grilled over charcoal are a classic Portuguese dish.

entities.name: Baking
entities.fact: Baking cooks fish in the dry heat of an oven, often wrapped or with a little liquid to keep it moist.

entities.name: Smoking
entities.fact: Smoking preserves and flavours fish with wood smoke, as in smoked salmon, kippers and smoked haddock.

entities.name: Canning
entities.fact: Canning seals fish in airtight tins and has long been used for sardines, tuna and salmon.

entities.name: Salting
entities.fact: Salting draws water out of fish so that bacteria cannot thrive, and it was the key to the medieval cod trade.

entities.name: Poaching
entities.fact: Poaching cooks fish gently in barely simmering liquid, such as a seasoned stock or milk.

entities.name: Pickling
entities.fact: Pickling preserves fish in vinegar or brine, as with the herring of northern Europe.

entities.name: Drying
entities.fact: Drying removes water from fish so that it will keep for months, and people have done this for thousands of years.

entities.name: Steaming
entities.fact: Steaming cooks fish gently over simmering water and is the classic method for whole fish in Cantonese cooking.

entities.name: Boiling
entities.fact: Boiling cooks fish in water at a full bubble, and it is the usual method for shellfish like lobster and crab.

entities.name: Pan-frying
entities.fact: Pan-frying cooks fish in a little oil or butter in a shallow pan, giving the skin a crisp finish.

entities.name: Deep-frying
entities.fact: Deep-frying submerges battered or breaded fish in very hot oil so that it cooks fast with a crisp coating.

entities.name: Curing
entities.fact: Curing preserves fish with salt, and sometimes sugar and spices, as in the Scandinavian gravlax.

entities.name: Freezing
entities.fact: Freezing preserves fish, and the American inventor Clarence Birdseye developed quick-freezing after watching the Inuit freeze fish in Labrador.

entities.name: Brining
entities.fact: Brining soaks fish in salt water before cooking or smoking, helping it keep moisture and flavour.

entities.name: Roasting
entities.fact: Roasting cooks whole fish or large cuts in an oven or over a fire, often with herbs and lemon.

entities.name: Barbecuing
entities.fact: Barbecuing cooks fish over hot coals or a flame, and whole fish are often held in a hinged basket so they do not break up.

entities.name: Braising
entities.fact: Braising cooks fish slowly in a small amount of liquid in a covered pan.

entities.name: Stewing
entities.fact: Stewing simmers fish in a flavoured liquid, as in bouillabaisse and other fishermen's stews.

entities.name: Serving raw
entities.fact: Serving fish raw, as in sashimi, poke or tartare, depends on fish that is very fresh or has been frozen first.

entities.name: En papillote
entities.fact: Cooking en papillote bakes fish sealed in a folded parcel of parchment paper, steaming it in its own juices.

entities.name: Blackening
entities.fact: Blackening coats fish in spices and sears it in a very hot pan, and Louisiana chef Paul Prudhomme made blackened redfish famous in the 1980s.

entities.name: Plank cooking
entities.fact: Plank cooking bakes or grills fish on a soaked wooden plank, a Pacific Northwest tradition used for salmon.

entities.name: Salt baking
entities.fact: Salt baking encases a whole fish in a crust of salt that traps moisture, and it is a classic way to cook sea bream.
